title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§8.5, Grothendieck's notes on torsion in crystalline cohomology, late 1960s; Katz, the Woods Hole formula and Serre's Mexico example are cited on this page or the next). k is algebraically closed of characteristic p and W = W(k). X is smooth projective of dimension n, embedded in P^r. Y runs over sections of X by hypersurfaces of degree d, parametrized by an open U_d. E(Y) is the crystalline vanishing (evanescent) cohomology of Y in the critical degree n-1, and E(Y,O_Y) is its Hodge/Hasse-Witt analogue. The subscript ss denotes the Frobenius-bijective ('semisimple', stable) part of a k-space with a p-linear endomorphism. (8.5.1) is an exact sequence relating (E(Y)⊗k)_ss to E(Y,O_Y)_ss through a 'fundamental homomorphism' φ. Its kernel and cokernel are controlled by maps v, w built from the p-torsion of the crystalline cohomology of X in degrees n-1 and n.

The page does four things.
(1) A struck-out equivalence: φ is surjective (resp. injective) for all d and s in U_d iff the same holds for one fixed d divisible by p with Ker v = 0, iff (Tors^{n-1}(X)⊗_W k)_ss = 0 (resp. (Tors^n(X)⊗_W k)_ss = 0).
(2) New numbered item 8.5.11, 'φ n'est pas bijectif'. Inequality (8.5.11.1) states, in any degree i, dim_k H^i(X,O)_ss = dim_{F_p} H^i(X_et, Z/p) ≥ dim((H^i_crys/Tors)⊗k)_ss. The equality is Artin-Schreier (H^i(X,Z/p)⊗k ≅ H^i(X,O)_ss). The right side is the multiplicity of slope 0, i.e. the rank of H^i_et(X,Z_p)/tors. Hence the gap measures p-torsion in étale (and so crystalline) cohomology. Bijectivity of φ (for i=n-1) is said to be equivalent to equality.
(3) Serre's Mexico example. X = (complete intersection)/(Z/p acting freely), cut down by hyperplanes to a surface (Lefschetz preserves π_1). It has H^1_crys = 0 but H^1(X,Z/p) ≅ Z/p. By 8.1.2, (Tors_p^2(X))_ss ≅ H^1(X,Z/p)⊗k = Ker φ, which is nonzero for every d and every Y. So φ need not be injective, already for n = 2.
(4) A struck-out attempt at non-surjectivity. Take X' = X × Z with Z smooth projective of dimension n-2, crystalline cohomology torsion-free and (H^{n-4}(Z)⊗k)_ss ≠ 0. Assuming a crystalline Künneth formula, (Tors^{n-1}(X')⊗k)_ss ≠ 0, giving non-surjective φ for n ≥ 4. Grothendieck adds that n = 3 examples probably exist 'en cherchant bien'.

The purpose is to measure how far Frobenius-semisimple vanishing cohomology mod p fails to be captured by the Hasse-Witt part. This feeds §8.6: mod-p monodromy of the unit-root part over U_d, a Chebotarev argument, and the congruences card Y(k') mod p.
errors: The marginal suggestion 'par exemple P_k^{n-2} si n pair' fails in general. Crystalline Frobenius acts on H^{2j}(P^m) as p^j, so (H^{2j}(P^m)⊗k)_ss = 0 for j > 0. P^{n-2} gives (H^{n-4}⊗k)_ss ≠ 0 only when n = 4. This may be one reason the passage was crossed out.

Possible degree slip in the X×Z construction. For Serre's surface X, the Frobenius-bijective torsion lives in Tors^2 (coming from H^1_et(Z/p)). Tors^3 should have zero ss part, since H^3_et(X,Z/p) = 0 for a proper surface and Tors^3 is Frobenius-twisted dual to Tors^2. By Künneth, the useful component of Tors^{n-1}(X×Z) is then Tors^2(X)⊗H^{n-3}(Z), not Tors^3(X)⊗H^{n-4}(Z). If so, n = 3 is immediate: Z a curve, using H^0(Z) where F is the identity. That would contradict the remark that n = 3 examples need 'cherchant bien'. This assumes the indexing of condition c) is as written; the previous page's indexing is ambiguous.

The equivalence 'φ bijective ⇔ equality in (8.5.11.1)' is stated without proof. It relies on 8.1.2/8.4.3 and the unverified condition Ker v = 0 (8.5.7). Künneth in crystalline cohomology was not yet available (Grothendieck flags this himself).

ideas.what: dim H^i(X,O)_ss = dim_{F_p} H^i_et(X,Z/p) ≥ dim((H^i_crys/Tors)⊗k)_ss; the gap is detected by p-torsion
ideas.modern_name: Artin-Schreier comparison plus slope-0 (unit-root) part of crystalline cohomology vs étale Z_p-cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Mexico 1956/58) for Artin-Schreier/Hasse-Witt; Bloch, Illusie (de Rham-Witt, 1979) for slope-0 = H_et(Z_p)⊗W

ideas.what: Serre's free Z/p-quotient example used to exhibit nonzero Frobenius-bijective p-torsion in H^2_crys of a surface
ideas.modern_name: Torsion in crystalline cohomology from p-torsion in π_1 / H^1_fl(μ_p) vs H^1_et(Z/p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (example); Illusie, Ekedahl (systematic theory of crystalline torsion)

ideas.what: Criterion for (non)bijectivity of the map from crystalline to Hasse-Witt semisimple vanishing cohomology of hypersurface sections, in terms of ss-parts of Tors^{n-1}, Tors^n of X
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root part of vanishing cohomology in Lefschetz pencils / families of hypersurface sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not clearly treated in the literature in this form (closest: Katz's work on unit-root F-crystals and p-adic monodromy)

ideas.what: Products X×Z with torsion-free Z to propagate torsion via a (conjectural) crystalline Künneth formula

missed.claim: The map φ from Frobenius-semisimple crystalline vanishing cohomology of hypersurface sections Y⊂X to their Hasse-Witt semisimple part is studied. Its kernel/cokernel are identified with ss-parts of p-torsion of H_crys(X). Grothendieck gives explicit examples of non-injectivity and attempts non-surjectivity. This 'unit-root vanishing cohomology' framework is a precursor to the mod-p monodromy question of §8.6, and its torsion obstruction does not seem to have been written up.
missed.quote: (Tors_p^2(X))_ss ≃ H^1(X,Z/pZ)⊗k = Ker φ (quel que soit d et la section Y de X de degré d, permettant de définir φ), qui est non nul, donc φ n'est pas injectif.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mod-p monodromy of Hasse-Witt / unit-root parts in families of hypersurface sections remains little studied, compared with p-rank strata of curves or abelian varieties. The page isolates crystalline torsion of the ambient variety as the correction term. This could matter for anyone studying such monodromy for non-simply-connected X.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a careful but mostly routine application of Artin-Schreier/slope-zero comparisons and Serre's classical example. Its context, the unit-root part of vanishing cohomology preparing a mod-p monodromy/Chebotarev conjecture, is of mild historical interest. The constructive part is crossed out and appears to contain a degree slip.
transcription_corrections: 'H^1(X,Z/pZ)≠Z/' should read 'H^1(X,Z/pZ) ≃ Z/pZ'. The symbol is an isomorphism sign, and in Serre's example H^1(X,Z/p) is Z/p, not 'different from'.
The marginal insertion over the struck words reads 'H^1(X,O)_ss' with a '||' beneath it, indicating H^1(X,O)_ss equals the following expression.
The handwritten insertion near 8.5.11 in the margin reads 'φ n'est pas bijectif', so the sentence becomes 'Si φ n'est pas bijectif'/'8.5.11. φ n'est pas bijectif ...'.
'Tors_p^2(X)' carries a struck-out '⊗k' with a handwritten 2 over the original exponent, as transcribed.
